name: standing stone

attributes.attribute: a single pillar erected by the Megalithic people
an early people with great engineering skill
some stand alone, some open a stone circle

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A standing stone is a mythic site. A single pillar of stone rises alone in a field. Many of these stones still stand across the old Celtic lands. An earlier people put them there. They belong to the Megalithic Civilization, and they are about six thousand years old. The stones show the skill of that early people and their deep sense of the sacred. They did not only place the stones. They joined them into circles and carved them, and their work still stands. Such monuments speak of a people who could shape stone with great care. A stone standing alone could mark a place of power. A group of stones could make a circle (see stone circles). The same builders raised the tombs called dolmens.
